findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-interop-fig/src/kiwi.rs:513-526 (inflate_raw), :530-548 (zstd_decode), :486-488 (trailing check only on the decompressed message)
findings.evidence: The kiwi.rs module doc says a census is produced 'only when the entire message decodes (never partial)'. The trailing-byte check covers only the decompressed message. Compressed bytes after the end of the raw-deflate stream (miniz decompress_to_vec_with_limit does not report unconsumed input) or after the first zstd frame (ruzstd StreamingDecoder reads one frame) are ignored without a loss entry. A chunk carrying a second frame would yield a census of the first frame reported as complete. miniz/ruzstd consumption behaviour was not run here (UNVERIFIED), hence PLAUSIBLE.
findings.remediation: Refuse (soft loss) when the compressed chunk has bytes after the stream/frame end; add a two-frame test

findings.evidence: decode_schema skips the duplicate-value check for structs. census then finds sessionID/localID by comparing each guid struct field's value with the key values. If several guid fields share a value, the wrong field is read as a varuint (a string or array field then misparses the rest), or session is overwritten and local stays None. That gives a wrong census or a soft failure from a crafted schema rather than a typed schema error. The impact is limited to a non-authoritative census.
findings.remediation: Match guid fields by identity (std::ptr::eq) or refuse duplicate struct field values in the schema
